### Given Data:
* Solid: Cylinder
* Base Diameter ($d$) $= 50\text{ mm}$, Axis Height ($h$) $= 60\text{ mm}$, resting on H.P.
* Cutting Plane: Auxiliary Vertical Plane (A.V.P.) inclined at $60^	ext{o}$ to reference line, passing at a distance of $17\text{ mm}$ from the axis.

### Step 1: Projections of the Cylinder (Initial Views)
* **Top View:** A circle of diameter $50\text{ mm}$. Divide the circle into $12$ equal parts and mark points $1, 2, \dots, 12$.
* **Front View:** A rectangle of dimensions $50\text{ mm}$ (base) $\times 60\text{ mm}$ (height).

### Step 2: Sectional Front View & Top View
1. In the top view, draw the cutting plane line (A.V.P.) as an edge view (a line inclined at $60^	ext{o}$) passing $17\text{ mm}$ away from the center.
2. Project the intersection points of the cutting plane with the generator lines onto the front view.
3. Connect these projected points with a smooth curve in the front view and hatch the sectional area (Sectional Front View).

### Step 3: True Shape of the Section
1. Draw an auxiliary reference line ($X_1Y_1$) parallel to the cutting plane trace.
2. Project perpendicular lines from the cutting points in the front view onto the auxiliary reference line.
3. Transfer the respective distances from the top view (measured from the central axis to the points) onto the corresponding projectors in the auxiliary view.
4. Join the points symmetrically to obtain the **True Shape** (which is an ellipse).
proTip: For cylinders and cones, always divide the base circle into 12 parts in the top view to get sufficient points for plotting accurate section curves.
